answer: Each agent must lock a deposit before it can submit a task bid; the protocol caps how much one deposit can buy in voting weight and slashs it when a randomly audited task proves fraudulent. Creating a thousand identities therefore does not create a thousand cheap votes: the attacker must tie up capital in each deposit and risks losing it on fabricated work. The tundra, karst, and ferrous task markets can vary in subject, but all enforce the same stake-and-audit rule.
